research_question: In adults aged 65 years and older with cancer, what is the effect of immune checkpoint inhibitors added to platinum-based chemotherapy, compared with platinum-based chemotherapy alone (with or without placebo), on overall survival at any time point?
treatment_label: Immune checkpoint inhibitor plus platinum-based chemotherapy
control_label: Platinum-based chemotherapy alone (with or without placebo)
outcome_description: Overall survival (time from randomisation to death from any cause) in the subgroup of participants aged 65 years and older, reported at any time point / data cut-off. The effect estimate is the trial's own reported hazard ratio for overall survival in the older-age subgroup (log[HR] with standard error, or HR with 95% confidence interval), taken directly from the published survival analysis (Cox model / stratified log-rank). Include open-ended older-age subgroups (e.g. '≥65 years', '65 years or older'), not narrower bands with an upper bound.
positive_direction: A positive effect size means adding immune checkpoint inhibitors to platinum-based chemotherapy improved overall survival in people aged 65 and older — i.e. a lower hazard of death (HR < 1) compared with chemotherapy alone.
search_queries: immune checkpoint inhibitor plus platinum chemotherapy randomized trial overall survival elderly
PD-1 PD-L1 inhibitor chemotherapy versus chemotherapy alone older patients 65 years subgroup survival
pembrolizumab atezolizumab durvalumab nivolumab chemotherapy trial hazard ratio overall survival age subgroup
inclusion_criteria: Clinical trial or comparative study in cancer patients comparing an immune checkpoint inhibitor combined with platinum-based chemotherapy against chemotherapy alone (with or without placebo)
Reports overall survival data (hazard ratio with CI/SE, or data allowing an HR to be derived) for participants aged 65 years and older, either as a subgroup or as a wholly older-adult population
Any cancer type, any line of therapy, any publication year or language, including conference abstracts and subgroup/pooled analyses of randomised trials
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study (systematic review, meta-analysis, narrative review, editorial, commentary, opinion piece, or purely theoretical/modelling paper)
No comparison between an ICI-plus-chemotherapy arm and a chemotherapy-alone (or chemotherapy-plus-placebo) control arm, e.g. single-arm studies or ICI-monotherapy versus chemotherapy comparisons only
No quantitative outcome data from which an effect size can be computed (no HR with CI/SE, no survival curve or event/person-time data, no means+SDs, t/F values, proportions or odds ratios)

Completely unrelated to the research topic (not about immune checkpoint inhibitors with platinum chemotherapy and survival), or reports only a narrow age band with an upper bound (e.g. 65-74 years) with no open-ended ≥65 estimate
moderators_to_extract: Specific ICI agent and target (PD-1, PD-L1, CTLA-4)
Trial sample size in the older-age subgroup
Risk of bias / blinding (placebo-controlled vs open-label) and publication year
effect_size_note: Extract the trial-reported hazard ratio for overall survival in the ≥65-year subgroup directly (log[HR] + SE, or HR with 95% CI converted to log[HR] and SE). Pool on the log-HR scale with inverse-variance random effects; HR < 1 favours ICI plus chemotherapy. Where multiple data cut-offs exist, use the most mature reported analysis; do not split by timepoint.
